title: Exact Quantum Values and Permutation-Blind Maximizers in Cyclic Bell Inequalities
impact_reason: Proves the sharp first-family quantum value in all dimensions, including commuting operators, and a support multiplicity theorem; explicit exact maximizers show scalar maximal Bell value need not certify uniform joint randomness. This consolidates two earlier standalone notes.
lay_summary: A Bell test can reach its exact quantum maximum while still producing biased joint outcomes; the same paper determines the maximum exactly.
surprise_reason: The score fixes equality phases but cannot see their cyclic order, so maximally violating devices can produce different output tables.
publication_reason: The consolidated presentation has a clear exact-bound theorem and a consequential certification counterexample. Credited family definitions, canonical strategy and second-family SOS are external. Check overlap with the separate permutation-blind Bell paper before treating both as independent submissions.
exact_gap: No new proof gap identified during triage; complete maximizing-face classification, worst-case guessing probability and robust bounds remain open. Exactness of canonical full-behavior randomness is not challenged.
next_step: Use as the canonical cyclic-family submission, with the scalar-versus-full-behavior distinction and the finite-dimensional scope of support rigidity prominent.
claim_boundary: Exact first cyclic operator value for q/qa/qc; support multiplicity only for attained finite-dimensional tensor maximizers; biased maximizers of both augmented families for d≥4; no exact optimal guessing probability or canonical-behavior refutation.

title: Maximal violation without maximal global randomness in a cyclic Bell family
impact_reason: Constructs nonuniform exact maximizers in every dimension d≥4, refuting a scalar Bell-value randomness implication while preserving uniform marginals. The result is incorporated into the later consolidated cyclic Bell paper.
lay_summary: Maximum violation of this Bell score does not by itself guarantee the largest possible joint randomness.
surprise_reason: Every local output remains uniform, but joint probabilities become biased at the same quantum maximum.
publication_reason: Substantive result, but the Aug9 consolidated paper includes and strengthens it; retain this record for provenance, not as another independent current contribution.
exact_gap: No separate mathematical gap inferred; worst-case guessing probability is only bounded below, and fixed canonical full-behavior randomness is outside the counterexample.
next_step: Cite the consolidated cyclic Bell paper and preserve this historical standalone version in the inventory.
claim_boundary: Explicit finite-dimensional strategies for d≥4, trivial Eve already sufficient; no conclusion for all maximizers at d=2,3 or a contradiction to fixed-full-behavior numerical certificates.

title: A Reciprocal-Square Obstruction for Equal-Sum–Product Matrices
impact_reason: An elementary reciprocal-square obstruction excludes every globally distinct positive-integer equal-sum/product matrix with at least three rows, uniformly in all dimensions. It resolves a precisely stated recreational conjecture without bounded search.
lay_summary: Only two rows can work in a matrix of distinct positive integers whose row sums and column products all equal the same number.
surprise_reason: The supposed equality gives 3 on one side and less than 2 on the other through a short reciprocal-square estimate.
publication_reason: A polished elementary recreational-mathematics note is plausible if historical novelty is confirmed. The proof is short and the two-row control makes its sharp scope understandable. Current inventory finds public repository publication but no Zenodo match.
exact_gap: No new proof gap identified on reading; no exhaustive current priority search was performed, and authorship is inferred from the project source because the PDF has no named author on its first page.
next_step: Confirm intended author metadata, preserve the exact distinctness/positivity assumptions and present to a venue receptive to elementary recreational results.
claim_boundary: Finite positive-integer matrices with global pairwise distinctness and common row sum equal to common column product; repeated entries and unequal sum/product constants behave differently.

title: Low-Schmidt rigidity and tensor-local constraints in the exceptional unitary Hecke Yang–Baxter class
impact_reason: Derives all-level tower multiplicities and low-operator-Schmidt-rank rigidity in the exceptional Hecke class. It shows abstract multiplicity arithmetic permits all even dimensions and forces any forbidden-mod-four rank-four candidate into simultaneous sandwich degeneracy.
lay_summary: The paper narrows where a missing Yang–Baxter operator could hide, while proving that several tempting representation-theoretic tests cannot resolve its existence.
surprise_reason: Abstract trace and multiplicity data impose no extra factor of two; any real obstruction must come from repeatedly realizing one local tensor.
publication_reason: A substantial set of structural partial results that could stand as a specialist constraints paper. It does not solve the exceptional spectrum, and its many mechanisms should be organized around the strongest low-rank rigidity theorem.
exact_gap: The d≡2 mod4 existence question, including d=6, remains open. Rank-four simultaneous-degeneracy and a one-sided rank-four square restriction in d=6 are not excluded. No fresh proof or verifier replay performed.
next_step: Independently audit the low-Schmidt control reduction and joint-sandwich identities; isolate complete theorems from ansatz exclusions.
claim_boundary: Exceptional unitary two-eigenvalue Hecke Yang–Baxter class q=e^(iπ/3), balanced projection; low OSR≤3 classification and conditional rank-four obstruction only, not complete spectrum or all d=4 solutions.
